2c: Al-ʿaṣr can name a long span or era, the part of a day near evening, and the prayer performed at that time takes its name from it.  · terms: العصر الدهر, al-ʿaṣr al-dahr, العصر العشي, al-ʿaṣr al-ʿashiyy, صلاة العصر, ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1
2d: The definite article in al-ʿaṣr points to a known time, but the verse does not choose among afternoon, the age in which people live, or time itself, leaving these senses to be heard together.  · terms: وَٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1

## ¶3
3a: Modern Turkish separates the senses: asır means a hundred years and asri means contemporary, while the day's late afternoon is called ikindi.
3b: The Turkish word asır does not evoke afternoon's fading light or the root's images of squeezing, refuge, and whirlwind.  · terms: العصر, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1
3c: The verse's al-ʿaṣr holds the hour and the era together, so the end of a day and the end of a lifetime bear one name.  · terms: وَٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1

## ¶4
4a: Arabic uses the dual al-ʿaṣrān for two paired limits of the day: night and day, or early morning and evening.  · terms: العصران الليل والنهار, al-ʿaṣrān al-layl wa-l-nahār, العصران الغداة والعشي, al-ʿaṣrān al-ghadāh wa-l-ʿashiyy
4b: The phrase bi-l-ghadāti wa-l-ʿashiyy in 6:52 is cited as the Qurʾān naming the morning-and-evening pair that Arabic calls the two ʿaṣrs.  · terms: بِٱلْغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلْعَشِىِّ, bi-l-ghadāti wa-l-ʿashiyy, العصران, al-ʿaṣrān  · verses: 6:52
4c: The phrase ṭarafay al-nahār in 11:114 is cited as the Qurʾān's wording for the day's two edges, corresponding to the paired limits called al-ʿaṣrān.  · terms: طَرَفَىِ ٱلنَّهَارِ, ṭarafay al-nahār, العصران, al-ʿaṣrān  · verses: 11:114
4d: Calling both ends of the day al-ʿaṣr shows the word grasping time at the entry or exit of a period; afternoon is its closing edge.  · terms: العصر, al-ʿaṣr, العصران, al-ʿaṣrān  · verses: 103:1

## ¶5
5a: The expression jāʾanī fulān ʿaṣran describes someone arriving late and slowly.  · terms: جاءني فلان عصرا, jāʾanī fulān ʿaṣran
5b: The phrase nāma wa-mā nāma li-ʿaṣr means that someone slept but did not sleep even for a moment; al-ʿaṣār can also mean a while.  · terms: نام وما نام لعصر, nāma wa-mā nāma li-ʿaṣr, العصار الحين, al-ʿaṣār al-ḥīn
5c: The word spans both a long era and a fleeting moment, and both an ordinary part of the day and the time of a delayed arrival.  · terms: العصر, al-ʿaṣr, جاءني فلان عصرا, jāʾanī fulān ʿaṣran, العصار, al-ʿaṣār
5d: The same word refers to a young woman's age of youth and maturity, and also to a person's lifespan and old age.  · terms: بلغت عصر شبابها وإدراكها, balaghat ʿaṣra shabābihā wa-idrākihā, العصر, al-ʿaṣr
5e: Late afternoon has the least time left in the day, as work nears its end and light fades; al-ʿaṣr therefore carries a feeling of lateness and dwindling time within the hour.  · terms: العصر, al-ʿaṣr

## ¶6
6a: In 79:42 the question about the Hour is answered in 79:46 by reducing a lifetime, as seen from the Hour, to the span of one evening or one forenoon.  · terms: ٱلسَّاعَةِ, al-sāʿah, عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا, ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā  · verses: 79:42, 79:46
6b: Although 79:46 does not use al-ʿaṣr, its ʿashiyy (evening) is treated as the afternoon sense that explains al-ʿaṣr; viewed from the end, the long era becomes an afternoon.  · terms: عَشِيَّةً, ʿashiyyah, العصر, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 79:46, 103:1
6c: The plea in 35:37 to be returned for good work is met with the reminder that people had already been granted a lifespan in which anyone who would reflect could do so.  · terms: أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُم, a-wa-lam nuʿammirkum, مَا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ, mā yatadhakkaru fīhi man tadhakkar  · verses: 35:37
6d: The time granted for reflection is the span in which the loss of 103:2 and the faith and good works of 103:3 take place.  · terms: خُسْرٍ, khusr, إِيمَان, īmān, عَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَات, ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt  · verses: 35:37, 103:2

## ¶7
7a: The concrete meaning of the root is to press something until liquid is made to flow from it.  · terms: ضغط شيء حتى يتحلب, ḍaghṭ shayʾin ḥattā yataḥallab, عصر, ʿaṣara
7b: Grapes were pressed in a feed-bag-like sack; the sack holds the grapes while hand or weight crushes them, and the juice drains through its weave. The device and place for pressing have names from this process.  · terms: المعصار, al-miʿṣār, المعصرة, al-miʿṣarah
7c: The liquid that runs off a pressing is called ʿuṣārah, and anything whose water is squeezed out is called ʿaṣīr.  · terms: العصارة, al-ʿuṣārah, كل شيء عصر ماؤه فهو عصير, kullu shayʾin ʿuṣira māʾuhu fa-huwa ʿaṣīr
7d: What remains in the sack is pulp, so pressing divides a thing into a flowing essence and a dry mass left behind.  · terms: العصارة, al-ʿuṣārah

## ¶8
8a: Arabic speakers made the flowing essence of a pressing a figure for goodness and giving; a generous person is described with the verb ʿaṣara, and ʿuṣārah can mean the yield from land.  · terms: العصارة والمعتصر, al-ʿuṣārah wa-l-muʿtaṣar, يعصر فينا كالذي تعصر, yaʿṣiru fīnā ka-lladhī taʿṣir, العصارة الغلة, al-ʿuṣārah al-ghallah
8b: Clouds that bring rain are described as being squeezed or as dripping, and a group that receives rain is said to have been ʿuṣira.  · terms: المعصرات, al-muʿṣirāt, السحابة المعصر, al-saḥābah al-muʿṣir, عصر القوم, ʿuṣira al-qawm
8c: The Qurʾān's al-muʿṣirāt in 78:14 is read as rain-bearing, squeezed clouds, with the water they pour beginning a sequence that brings forth grain, plants, and layered gardens in 78:15–16.  · terms: مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ, min al-muʿṣirāt, مَآءًۭ ثَجَّاجًۭا, māʾan thajjājā, حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا, ḥabban wa-nabātan, جَنَّٰتٍ أَلْفَافًا, jannātin alfāfā  · verses: 78:14, 78:15, 78:16
8d: The paragraph reads 78:14–16 as a chain of blessing: squeezed cloud, then grain and vegetation, then gardens.  · terms: ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ, al-muʿṣirāt, حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا, ḥabban wa-nabātan, جَنَّٰتٍ أَلْفَافًا, jannātin alfāfā  · verses: 78:14, 78:15, 78:16

## ¶9
9a: A tongue dried by thirst is called maʿṣūr, as if it had been squeezed until no water remained.  · terms: المعصور اللسان اليابس عطشا, al-maʿṣūr al-lisān al-yābis ʿaṭshan
9b: Iʿtiṣār can describe someone clearing a stuck morsel by drinking water in small sips, so squeezing here names a movement of rescue.  · terms: الاعتصار, al-iʿtiṣār, يعتصر بالماء, yaʿtaṣiru bi-l-māʾ
9c: The poet reverses that rescue image: if his throat were blocked by something other than water, he could clear it with water, implying that water itself blocks him and no further sip can save him.  · terms: لو بغير الماء حلقي شرق, law bi-ghayr al-māʾ ḥalqī shariq, بالماء اعتصاري, bi-l-māʾ iʿtiṣārī

## ¶10
10a: Set beside the verse's time sense, these root images make time look like pressure that extracts something from a person: it may leave a flowing essence that becomes generosity, or only a dry mass and a thirst-dried tongue.  · terms: العصر, al-ʿaṣr, المعصور, al-maʿṣūr, العصارة, al-ʿuṣārah  · verses: 103:1
10b: The loss in 103:2 is identified with the leftover side of what has been squeezed, and the surah's final word ṣabr is linked to the bitter essence squeezed from a tree, carrying the pressure image through to 103:3.  · terms: خُسْرٍ, khusr, صبر, ṣabr  · verses: 103:2

## ¶11
11a: Joseph's imprisonment in 12:35 is bounded by an indefinite period, which the paragraph connects to al-ʿaṣr as a time-span and as detention, while stressing that the Qurʾān uses a different word for prison.  · terms: حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ, ḥattā ḥīn, العصر, al-ʿaṣr, الحبس, al-ḥabs  · verses: 12:35
11b: In 12:36 the young prisoner's dream uses ʿaṣara for pressing grapes but names the pressed product, wine, rather than the grapes.  · terms: أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, aʿṣiru khamran  · verses: 12:36
11c: Joseph interprets the dream as the young man serving wine to his master, and the following verse identifies him as the one expected to be released from prison.  · terms: فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًۭا, fa-yasqī rabbahu khamran, نَاجٍۢ, nājin  · verses: 12:41, 12:42
11d: The dictionary sense of al-ʿaṣr as a place of rescue is echoed by the scene: the one who squeezes in his dream is the prisoner who gets out.  · terms: العصر المنجاة, al-ʿaṣr al-manjāh, أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, aʿṣiru khamran, نَاجٍۢ, nājin  · verses: 12:36, 12:42

## ¶12
12a: The released prisoner forgets Joseph, leaving Joseph in prison for several years; the prisoner remembers him only after a long interval.  · terms: فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ, fa-labitha fī al-sijni biḍʿa sinīn, بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ, baʿda ummah  · verses: 12:42, 12:45
12b: Joseph turns the king's dream of green and dry ears into a schedule: first seven years of planting, with most of the harvest left in its ear for storage.  · terms: سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍۢ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍۢ, sunbulātin khuḍrin wa-ukhar yābisāt, فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ, fa-dharūhu fī sunbulih  · verses: 12:43, 12:47
12c: The paragraph connects the Arab crop term ʿaṣara, used when the ear's husks appear, with ʿaṣr as protection: the grain is held safe inside its husk, although the Qurʾān here says sunbul, not ʿaṣr.  · terms: قد عصر الزرع, qad ʿaṣara al-zarʿ, العصر, al-ʿaṣr, الحرز, al-ḥirz, سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ, sunbulih  · verses: 12:47
12d: The seven hard years consume what was stored for them, except for a small amount the people preserve.  · terms: سَبْعٌۭ شِدَادٌۭ, sabʿun shidād, مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ, mā qaddamtum lahunna, تُحْصِنُونَ, tuḥṣinūn  · verses: 12:48
12e: The final year brings relief, and yaʿṣirūn in 12:49 is interpreted as people extracting a yield from their lands.  · terms: يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ, yughāthu al-nās, يَعْصِرُونَ, yaʿṣirūn  · verses: 12:49

## ¶13
13a: The Joseph story arranges several seemingly distant root senses on one calendar: imprisonment as a span, pressing in a dream, prolonged years of forgetting, grain sheltered in its husk, and pressing again in the year of abundance.  · terms: العصر, al-ʿaṣr, أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, aʿṣiru khamran, عصر الزرع, ʿaṣara al-zarʿ, يَعْصِرُونَ, yaʿṣirūn  · verses: 12:35, 12:36, 12:42, 12:47, 12:49
13b: In this account pressing marks the end of scarcity: the wine-producing grapes are the share of those who patiently waited through and stored for the hard years.  · terms: أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, aʿṣiru khamran, يَعْصِرُونَ, yaʿṣirūn, صبر, ṣabr  · verses: 12:36, 12:47, 12:48, 12:49
13c: The sworn time in 103:1 is presented as more than a period that consumes people: it can shelter what is stored within it and eventually let that store flow out.  · terms: وَٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1

## ¶14
14a: Al-ʿaṣr can mean detention or restraint; asking mā ʿaṣraka asks what held or prevented someone, and ʿāṣir describes a person who keeps a tight grip and does not give.  · terms: العصر الحبس, al-ʿaṣr al-ḥabs, ما عصرك أي ما منعك, mā ʿaṣaraka, mā manaʿaka, فلان عاصر إذا كان ممسكا, fulān ʿāṣir idhā kāna mumsikan
14b: The root is used for a father withholding a child's property and for taking back a gift after giving it.  · terms: يعتصر الوالد على ولده في ماله, yaʿtaṣiru al-wālidu ʿalā waladih fī mālih, فاعتصرتها, fa-iʿtaṣartuhā
14c: The same root can describe both generosity and stinginess: squeezing gives when what is held flows out, and hoards when the hand keeps hold of it.  · terms: يعصر فينا, yaʿṣiru fīnā, عاصر, ʿāṣir, العصر, al-ʿaṣr

## ¶15
15a: A young woman at her first menstruation is called al-muʿṣir because she is kept at home, with a protected place made for her.  · terms: المعصر ساعة تطمث, al-muʿṣir sāʿata taṭmith, العصر, al-ʿaṣr
15b: The grain kept inside its husk shares this sense of shelter; holding can protect something at a threshold rather than merely deprive it.  · terms: عصر الزرع, ʿaṣara al-zarʿ, الحرز, al-ḥirz

## ¶16
16a: In 68:17–18 the Qurʾān likens the deniers' test to garden owners who swear to gather their crop in the morning and make no exception.  · terms: أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ, aṣḥāb al-jannah, لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ, la-yaṣrimunnahā muṣbiḥīn, وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ, wa-lā yastathnūn  · verses: 68:17, 68:18
16b: The owners' purpose is to prevent any poor person from entering the garden to share its produce.  · terms: أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌۭ, an lā yadkhulannahā al-yawma ʿalaykum miskīn  · verses: 68:24
16c: While the owners sleep, a visitation from God ruins the garden; on seeing it they first think they have lost their way, then recognize that they have been deprived.  · terms: طَآئِفٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ, ṭāʾifun min rabbik, كَٱلصَّرِيمِ, ka-l-ṣarīm, إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ, innā la-ḍāllūn, مَحْرُومُونَ, maḥrūmūn  · verses: 68:19, 68:20, 68:26, 68:27
16d: The garden shows that a product kept back from others does not remain in its owner's hands; the owners' oath without exception is contrasted with this surah's oath followed by an exception in its third verse after the general judgment in the second.  · terms: لَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ, lā yastathnūn, وَٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr, خُسْرٍ, khusr, إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, illā alladhīna āmanū  · verses: 68:17, 103:1, 103:2

## ¶17
17a: The root can mean attaching oneself firmly to something, and al-ʿaṣr can name the place of refuge or shelter.  · terms: تعلق بشيء وامتساك به, taʿalluq bi-shayʾ wa-imtisāk bih, العصر الملجأ, al-ʿaṣr al-maljaʾ
17b: The verb forms iʿtaṣara and taʿaṣṣara describe taking refuge in a person, while iʿtaṣara bi-l-makān means seeking shelter in a place; ʿuṣrat al-manjūd names refuge for a distressed, trapped person.  · terms: اعتصرت بفلان وتعصرت, iʿtaṣartu bi-fulān wa-taʿaṣṣartu, اعتصر بالمكان, iʿtaṣara bi-l-makān, عصرة المنجود, ʿuṣrat al-manjūd
17c: The expression mā baynahumā ʿaṣr wa-lā yaṣr means that two people have neither affection nor kinship between them.  · terms: ما بينهما عصر ولا يصر, mā baynahumā ʿaṣr wa-lā yaṣr, مودة ولا قرابة, mawaddah wa-lā qarābah
17d: The paragraph gives ʿunṣur, meaning a person's stock or lineage, an etymology from refuge al-ʿaṣr with an added nūn.  · terms: العنصر والعنصر الأصل والحسب, al-ʿunṣur, al-ʿunṣur al-aṣl wa-l-ḥasab, العصر وهو الملجأ, al-ʿaṣr wa-huwa al-maljaʾ
17e: The armor term al-maʿāṣir is derived from al-ʿaṣr because armor encloses and protects its wearer.  · terms: المعاصر الدروع, al-maʿāṣir al-durūʿ, العصر, al-ʿaṣr

## ¶18
18a: Squeezing and refuge are reconciled as forms of grasping: squeezing closes around something from outside, while a person seeking refuge firmly holds onto a shelter, as armor encloses and protects the body.  · terms: العصر, al-ʿaṣr, الملجأ, al-maljaʾ, المعاصر, al-maʿāṣir
18b: The expression for a distressed person's refuge reinforces this link: the one pressed or overwhelmed runs to a shelter.  · terms: عصرة المنجود, ʿuṣrat al-manjūd, الملجأ, al-maljaʾ
18c: Heard beside the oath in 103:1, the time named by al-ʿaṣr appears both as a span that constrains people and as a place of refuge.  · terms: وَٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr, الملجأ, al-maljaʾ  · verses: 103:1

## ¶19
19a: The cave story is used to show how refuge can close or suspend the experience of time: the youths withdraw from their community's worship and are told to seek the cave and God's mercy.  · terms: فَأْوُۥٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ, faʾwū ilā al-kahf, إِذْ أَوَى ٱلْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ, idh awā al-fityatu ilā al-kahf  · verses: 18:16, 18:10
19b: Inside the cave the youths are made to sleep for counted years, but on waking they think they stayed only a day or part of one.  · terms: فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ, fa-ḍarabnā ʿalā ādhānihim, لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ, labithnā yawman aw baʿḍa yawm  · verses: 18:11, 18:19
19c: The story says they actually remained in the cave three hundred years and nine more; the paragraph hears refuge, a long era, and a duration mistaken for a moment together, although the word al-ʿaṣr itself is absent.  · terms: ثَلَٰثَ مِا۟ئَةٍۢ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُوا۟ تِسْعًۭا, thalātha miʾati sinīn wa-zdādū tisʿā, العصر, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 18:25
19d: The exception of believers in 103:3 is linked to the cave's refuge image, so escape from loss is heard as seeking shelter in a place.  · terms: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, illā alladhīna āmanū, العصر, al-ʿaṣr

## ¶20
20a: Iʿṣār names a wind that lifts dust from the ground and raises it toward the sky like a column; it can also name the dust as it rises in a spinning form.  · terms: الإعصار ريح تهب تثير الغبار, al-iʿṣār rīḥun tahubbu tuthīru al-ghubār, الإعصار الغبار الذي يسطع مستديرا, al-iʿṣār al-ghubār alladhī yasṭaʿu mustadīran
20b: This branch of the root depicts a moving wind gathering and turning what is on the ground, then pulling it upward into a column.  · terms: الإعصار, al-iʿṣār
20c: The same branch describes fragrance rising in the wake of a perfumed woman; ʿuṣrah is the scent's spreading and swelling.  · terms: مرت امرأة متطيبة لذيلها عصر, marrat imraʾatun mutaṭayyibatun li-dhaylihā ʿaṣr, العصرة, al-ʿuṣrah
20d: The paragraph groups dust and fragrance as two things that can billow upward behind something moving.  · terms: الإعصار, al-iʿṣār, العصرة, al-ʿuṣrah

## ¶21
21a: The paragraph reads 2:264–265 as contrasting showy spending, which is like soil washed from bare rock, with spending for God's approval, which is like a garden yielding abundantly under heavy or light rain.  · terms: صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ, ṣafwān ʿalayhi turāb, وَابِلٌ, wābil, جَنَّةٌ, jannah  · verses: 2:264, 2:265

#11 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء · reports · Critics cite the incident as sin: the Prophet expelled poor believers despite the prohibition, became one of the wrongdoers, contradicted Noah's refusal to expel believers and the command to follow prophets, sought worldly adornment, and later said God rebuked him. «احتج الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من وجوه»

#68 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · خباب بن الأرت · reports · A related report says the Prophet would rise and leave the poor believers, after which the instruction to remain with those who call on God was revealed. «وفي رواية عن خباب فإذا أراد أن يقوم قام وتركنا فأنزل الله تعالى واصبر نفسك»
#69 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عباس · reports · Al-ʿAwfi's report from Ibn ʿAbbas says nobles would believe if the poor were moved back so they could pray behind the nobles; expulsion meant moving them from the row, not the gathering. «وروى العوفي عن ابن عباس أن ناسا من الأشراف قالوا: نؤمن بك وإذا صلينا خلفك فأخر»
#70 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Despite variations in the reports, their common point is that Arab notables asked the Prophet to send the poor believers away, prompting the verse. «ومضمونها أن ناسا من أشراف العرب سألوا من الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم طرد فقراء المؤمنين عنه فنزلت»
#71 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · After commanding warning for the unpious, God honors the pious and forbids their expulsion, describing their outward and inward sincerity in worship. «ولما أمر تعالى بإنذار غير المتقين لعلهم يتقون أردف ذلك بتقريب المتقين وإكرامهم ونهاه عن طردهم»
#72 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عامر · reports · The majority read بالغداة; Ibn ʿAmir and several others read بالغدوة, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman is also reported without the final هاء, and Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads plural forms بالغدوات والعشيات. «وقرأ الجمهور بالغداة. وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو عبد الرحمن ومالك بن دينار والحسن ونصر بن عاصم وأبو رجاء العطاردي بالغدوة.»

#73 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الفراء · reports · The familiar form غدوة is treated as a proper noun and diptote; al-Farra reports a dialect that uses it for the morning of the same day. «والمشهور في غدوة أنها معرفة بالعلمية ممنوعة الصرف. قال الفراء: سمعت أبا»
#74 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Calling on their Lord means asking, seeking refuge, and directing supplication and desire to Him. «يدعون ربهم يسألونه ويلجأون إليه ويقصدونه بالدعاء والرغبة»
#75 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · prefers · Morning and evening stand for continual worship, like saying 'praise God morning and evening'; they may also be singled out because they are busy hours, making remembrance then especially telling. «بالغداة والعشي كناية عن الزمان الدائم ولا يراد بهما خصوص زمانهما»
#76 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الحسن · reports · Al-Hasan and Muqatil identify the phrase with the two daily prayers practiced in Mecca, morning and evening. «فقال الحسن ومقاتل: هي الصلاة بمكة التي كانت مرتين في اليوم بكرة وعشيا.»
#77 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · قتادة · reports · Qatada and Mujahid in one report identify the phrase as the dawn and afternoon prayers. «وقال قتادة ومجاهد: في رواية عنه هي صلاة الصبح والعصر.»
#78 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عمر · reports · Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid in another report, and Ibrahim identify the phrase with the five prayers. «وقال ابن عمر وابن عباس ومجاهد في رواية وإبراهيم: هي الصلوات الخمس.»
#79 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · بعض القصاص · reports · Some storytellers take it as people gathering with the believers morning and evening; Ibn al-Musayyib, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAmra, and others object that the verse concerns congregational prayers. «وقال بعض القصاص: إنه الاجتماع إليهم غدوة وعشيا فأنكر ذلك ابن المسيب وعبد الرحمن بن أبي عمرة وغيرهما،»
#80 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · أبو جعفر · reports · Abu Jaʿfar interprets it as reciting and learning the Qur'an. «وقال أبو جعفر: هي قراءة القرآن وتعلمه.»
#81 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الضحاك · reports · Al-Dahhak says it means worship; Ibrahim in another report says remembrance of God; al-Zajjaj says monotheistic, sincere supplication and worship. «وقال الضحاك: العبادة. وقال إبراهيم في رواية: ذكر الله. وقال الزجاج: دعاء الله تعالى بالتوحيد والإخلاص وعبادته.»
#82 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · أبو زيد · reports · Abu Zayd attests غدوة for the morning of the current day; Sibawayh and al-Khalil also report a dialect that declines it with tanwin. «حكى أبو زيد: لقيته فينة غير مصروف ولقيته الفينة بعد الفينة أي الحين بعد الحين»
#83 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhshari says the statement answers attacks on poor believers' sincerity: the Prophet must judge by their outward conduct, and each person bears their own account, as in the rule that no bearer bears another's burden. «قال الزمخشري: كقوله: إن حسابهم إلا على ربي وذلك أنهم طعنوا في دينهم وإخلاصهم»
#84 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's hypothetical that their inner state might be blameworthy, since God has already testified to their sincere intentions. «ولا يمكن ما ذكره من الترديد في قوله: وإن كان الأمر إلى آخره لأنه تعالى قد أخبر بأنهم»
#85 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · أبو عبيد · reports · Abu ʿUbayd faults Ibn ʿAmir and al-Sulami's reading as following the written waw, arguing that script does not prove pronunciation, as in صلاة and زكاة. «لما خفيت هذه اللغة على أبي عبيد أساء الظن بمن قرأ هذه القراءة»
#86 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · The author rebukes Abu ʿUbayd for ignorance of the dialect and reading transmission, defending the readers' competence and the principle that recitation is transmitted orally. «وهذا من أبي عبيد جهل بهذه اللغة التي حكاها سيبويه والخليل وقرأ بها هؤلاء الجماعة»
#87 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Al-ʿAshiyy is apparently synonymous with al-ʿashiyya, though it may be a collective; the cited verse uses it for late afternoon. «والظاهر أن العشي مرادف للعشية ألا ترى قوله: إذ عرض عليه بالعشي الصافنات الجياد»
#88 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ means they make their intentions sincere for God in worship; 'face' can denote a thing's essence and reality. «ومعنى يريدون وجهه يخلصون نياتهم له في عبادتهم ويعبر عن ذات الشيء وحقيقته بالوجه»
#89 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn ʿAbbas explains seeking God's face as seeking His reward. «وقال ابن عباس: يطلبون ثواب الله والجملة في موضع الحال وقد استدل بقوله:»
#90 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The phrase يريدون وجهه is circumstantial; theologians who use 'His face' to prove a bodily member are mistaken. «والجملة في موضع الحال وقد استدل بقوله: وجهه من أثبت الأعضاء لله تعالى الله عن ذلك»
#91 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الحسن · reports · Al-Hasan and the majority understand 'their reckoning' and 'your reckoning' as the reckoning of deeds. «قال الحسن والجمهور: الحساب هنا حساب الأعمال.»
#92 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الطبري · reports · Al-Tabari transmits an interpretation of reckoning as worldly provision: the Prophet neither provides for them nor they for him. «وقيل: حساب الأرزاق أي لا ترزقهم ولا يرزقونك حكاه الطبري.»
#93 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The first من is partitive and circumstantial: if it followed شيء it would be adjectival; عليک is the predicate under the Hijazi analysis, or the subject predicate otherwise. «ومن في من حسابهم وفي من حسابك مبعضة في موضع نصب على الحال في من حسابهم»
#94 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Making the second من حسابك circumstantial is weak because a semantic عامل cannot normally have its حال advanced before both itself and its possessor; other predicate analyses are also weak because عليهم carries the main information. «وأما في من حسابك فقيل: هو في موضع نصب على الحال ويضعف ذلك بأن الحال إذا كان العامل فيها معنى الفعل»
#95 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The two clauses honor the Prophet by placing him first both times, although the second could have been phrased with the believers first; this is reciprocal framing (رد العجز على الصدر). «وانظر إلى حسن اعتنائه تعالى بنبيه وتشريفه بخطابه حيث بدأ به في الجملتين معا»
#96 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The apparent فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ responds to the negation: since their reckoning is not the Prophet's concern, expulsion cannot follow from it; the first possible sense of ما تأتينا فتحدثنا does not fit. «أن قوله: فتطردهم جواب لقوله ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء يكون النصب هنا»
#97 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · prefers · فتكون is coordinated with فتطردهم, reporting the nonoccurrence of both expulsion and its consequence, wrongdoing. «والظاهر في قوله: فتكون من الظالمين أن يكون معطوفا على فتطردهم»
#98 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · Another parsing makes فتكون a response to the prohibition لا تطرد, with the two account clauses interrupting between prohibition and result. «أن يكون فتكون جوابا للنهي»
#99 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhshari says the paired clauses together mean that neither side is held to the other's reckoning, echoing the rule that no soul bears another's burden. «قال الزمخشري: (فإن قلت) : ما كفى قوله: ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء حتى ضم إليه ما من حسابك عليهم»
#100 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · The author says al-Zamakhshari's wording لا تؤاخذ أنت ولا هم بحساب صاحبه is ungrammatical because no singular antecedent supports its pronoun; he proposes clearer alternatives. «وقوله: كأنه قيل لا تؤاخذ أنت ولا هم بحساب صاحبه تركيب غير عربي»
#101 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · prefers · The apparent pronouns throughout the two clauses refer to the poor believers who call on God. «والظاهر أن الضمائر كلها عائدة على الذين يدعون»
#102 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhshari allows the pronouns to refer to the polytheists, making the clauses parenthetical: the Prophet's account is not theirs, so their belief should not lead him to expel believers. «وقيل: الضمير في من حسابهم وفي عليهم عائد على المشركين وتكون الجملتان اعتراضا بين النهي وجوابه»
#103 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عطية · reports · Ibn ʿAṭiyya likewise allows the pronouns to mean the disbelievers seeking the poor believers' expulsion, while تطردهم refers to the weak believers; the following ف supports a causal link. «وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يكون الضمير في حسابهم وعليهم للكفار الذين أرادوا طرد المؤمنين»
#104 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الطبري · reports · Al-Tabari says reckoning here concerns worldly provision, in which case all pronouns refer to the believers. «وحكى الطبري أن الحساب هنا إنما هو في رزق الدنيا أي لا ترزقهم ولا يرزقونك»
#105 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · On the prohibitive parsing, the account clauses and the response to the first are parenthetical before the result of the ban on expelling them. «وتكون الجملتان وجواب الأولى اعتراضا بين النهي وجوابه»
#106 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The unjust are people who put things in the wrong place. «ومعنى من الظالمين من الذين يضعون الشيء في غير مواضعه»
#107 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · العشي is indefinite; whether it is synonymous with feminine عشية or a collective like قمح/قمحة is disputed, and the first is likelier because 38:31 refers to one evening. «وأما " العشي " فنكرة وكذلك " عشية " وهل العشي مرادف لعشية؟»
#108 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · Regional codices all write الغدوة with wāw, but Ibn ʿĀmir’s reading rests on transmission, not spelling alone; forms such as الصلاة and الزكاة are read without wāw. «واتفقت مصاحف الأمصار على رسم هذه اللفظة " الغدوة " بالواو»
#109 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · غداة derives from غدوة by opening wāw and changing it to alif; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads plural الغدوات والعشيات, while another report has بالغدو with doubled wāw and no tāʾ. «وأصل غداة: غدوة، تحركت الواو وانفتح ما قبلها فقلبت ألفا.»
#110 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · سيبويه والخليل · reports · They report that some Arabs make غدوة indefinite with tanwin, comparable to ضحوة; Ibn ʿĀmir makes it indefinite and adds the article. «حكى سيبويه والخليل أن بعضهم ينكر فيقول " غدوة " بالتنوين،»
#111 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو علي الفارسي · reports · Abū ʿAlī allows the article on غدوة by treating a definite word as indefinite, like فينة when it means ‘time after time.’ «أبو علي الفارسي: " وجه دخول الألف واللام عليها أنه يجوز وإن كانت معرفة أن تنكر،»
<<part 2 ends; continues in part 3>>

#112 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو جعفر النحاس · reports · Al-Naḥḥās says غدوة is normally definite but may be indefinite and then take the article; he lists readers who use this form. «أبو جعفر النحاس: " قرأ أبو عبد الرحمن ومالك بن دينار وابن عامر: " بالغدوة "»
#113 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · مكي بن أبي طالب · reports · Makkī says غداة is always indefinite; most Arabs make غدوة definite, while a minority make it indefinite, supporting the reading. «مكي بن أبي طالب: " إنما دخلت الألف واللام على " غداة " لأنها نكرة،»
#114 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · يريدون is circumstantial from either the subject or object of يدعون; the subject analysis is correct, with omitted sense ‘they seek His face through their supplication at these times.’ «قوله: { يريدون } هذه الجملة في محل نصب على الحال من فاعل " يدعون "»
#115 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · In ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء, ما may govern an accusative predicate عليك, or be inactive with عليك a fronted predicate and من شيء its subject with extra من. «قوله: { ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء } " ما " هذه يجوز أن تكون الحجازية الناصبة للخبر»
#116 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · من حسابهم may be a partitive circumstantial phrase modifying شيء because a delayed modifier would be adjectival; it then depends on the implicit ‘being’ in عليك. «وقوله: { من حسابهم } قالوا: " من " بتعيضية وهي في محل نصب على الحال،»
#117 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · Alternatively من شيء is a subject raised by عليك under negation, with من حسابهم circumstantial; or من حسابهم is predicate and عليك circumstantial, though this last information structure is unclear. «ويجوز أن يكون " من شيء " في محل رفع بالفاعلية ورافعه " عليك " لاعتماده على النفي،»
#118 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · In the parallel clause من حسابك cannot readily be a circumstance before its semantic governor and owner, so it may be explanatory instead; its partitive sense is also unclear. «لا يجوز أن ينصب على الحال لأنه يلزم تقدمه على عامله المعنوي، وهو ضعيف أو ممتنع،»
#119 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · Addressing the Prophet first in both clauses honors him; the second could have repeated the first word order, but is rearranged in context. «وقدم خطابه عليه السلام في الجملتين تشريفا له،»
#120 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · The two clauses use the rhetorical figure رد الأعجاز على الصدور, also found in the cited proverb and poem. «وفي هاتين الجملتين ما يسميه أهل البديع: رد الأعجاز على الصدور،»
#121 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhsharī says the clauses together mean neither person is accountable for the other’s account, echoing 6:164; both are needed to express reciprocity. «ولا يستقل بهذا المعنى إلا الجملتان جميعا كأنه قيل: لا تؤاخد أنت ولا هم بحساب صاحبه»
#122 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الشيخ · rejects · Al-Shaykh calls al-Zamakhsharī’s wording ungrammatical because صاحبه lacks a compatible singular antecedent, whether the pronoun is read as third or second person. «تركيب غير عربي، لا يجوز عود الضمير هنا غائبا ولا مخاطبا،»
#123 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · The intended wording can be repaired by supplying كل واحد with أنت ولا هم appositional to it; however, the point is that each is not charged for another’s account. «والذي يظهر أن كلام الزمخشري صحيح، ولكن فيه حذف وتقديره: لا يؤاخذ كل واحد»
#124 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · The apparent reading returns all three pronouns to one group: those who call upon their Lord. «والضمائر الثلاثة، أعني التي في قوله: { من حسابهم }»
#125 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الطبري · reports · Al-Tabari also takes all three pronouns as referring to the worshippers, but understands their account as worldly provision. «وهم الذين يدعون ربهم، وبه قال الطبري، إلا أنه فسر الحساب بالرزق الدنيوي»
#126 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الزمخشري وابن عطية · reports · Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya refer the first two pronouns to the polytheists and the third to the worshippers. «وقال الزمخشري وبان عطية: " إن الضميرين الأولين يعودان على المشركين»
#127 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الشيخ · reports · Another view refers the pronouns in their account and upon them to the polytheists, making the two clauses parenthetical. «وقيل: الضمير في " حسابهم " و " عليهم " عائد على المشركين وتكون الجملتان اعتراضا»
#128 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · rejects · The two clauses can be parenthetical regardless of whom the first two pronouns refer to; they interrupt the prohibition and its result. «بل هما اعتراض بين النهي وهو " لا تطرد " وبين جوابه وهو فتكون»
#129 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · The subjunctive فتطردهم can answer the prohibition or express the consequence of the negated mutual accounting; the intended sense denies both expulsion and its cause. «ما يكون مؤاخذة كل واحد بحساب صاحبه فيكف يقع طرد؟»
#130 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · rejects · The alternative reading of the example, where the visit occurs but the conversation does not, does not suit this verse. «وهذا المعنى لا يليق بالآية الكريمة»
#131 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · فتكون is most clearly coordinated with فتطردهم, reporting expulsion and the injustice that results from it. «أظهرهما: أنه منصوب عطفا على " فتطردهم " والمعنى:»
#132 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhshari also allows coordination, treating being unjust as caused by expelling them. «قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن تكون عطفا على " فتطردهم "»
#133 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · مكي والواحدي وأبو البقاء · reports · Makki, al-Wahidi, and Abu al-Baqa mention فتكون as a response to the prohibition. «ولم يذكر مكي ولا الواحدي ولا أبو البقاء غيره»
#134 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو حيان · reports · Abu Hayyan compares this construction with the prohibition in Ta-Ha 20:61 and treats the intervening clauses as parenthetical. «قال الشيخ: " وجوزوا أن يكون " فتكون " جوابا»
#135 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · rejects · The parenthetical analysis does not depend on referring the first two pronouns to the polytheists. «قلت: قد تقدم أن كونهما اعتراضا لا يتوقف على عود الضميرين»
#136 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · Most read بالغداة; Ibn ʿĀmir and several named readers use بالغدوة with ḍamma, still dāl, and fatḥa on wāw, also in al-Kahf; غدوة is normally a proper-name form. «قرأ الجمهور: " بالغداة " هنا وفي الكهف وابن عامر: { بالغدوة } بضم الغين وسكون الدال»
#137 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الفراء · reports · Al-Farrāʾ says Arabs do not add the article to definite الغدوة and cites ‘غداة الخميس’; the author says this misses an indefinite dialect form. «قال: " ألا ترى أن العرب لا تضيفها، فكذا لا يدخلها الألف واللام، إنما يقولون: جئتك غداة الخميس "»
#138 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو عبيد · reports · Abū ʿUbayd attacks بالغدوة as copying the written wāw, which cannot establish pronunciation because الصلاة and الزكاة are written with wāw but pronounced without it. «إنما نرى ابن عامر والسلمي قرآ تلك القراءة إتباعا للخط، وليس في إثبات الواو في الكتاب دليل على القراءة بها،»
#139 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو علي الفارسي · reports · Abū ʿAlī prefers بالغداة: it can be indefinite or definite with the article, while غدوة is a proper name and should not take the article; its written wāw proves nothing. «الوجه قراءة العامة بالغداة، لأنها تستعمل نكرة ومعرفة بالام، فأما " غدوة " فمعرفة»
#140 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · rejects · The author rejects Abū ʿUbayd’s attack: these respected Arab readers are not presumed mistaken, and Sibawayh and al-Khalīl record indefinite غدوة. «إلا أن هذا الطعن لا يلتفت إليه، وكيف يظن بمن تقدم أنهم يلحنون،»
#141 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · سعيد بن المسيب ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة · reports · Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatada say the morning and evening invocation refers to the obligatory prayers. «قال سعيد بن المسيب، ومجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة: المراد بذلك الصلوات المكتوبات»
#142 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Invoking God means worshipping and asking Him; 40:60 similarly says to call upon God and He will respond. «وقوله {يدعون ربهم} أي: يعبدونه ويسألونه {بالغداة والعشي}»
#143 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Seeking God’s face means that these worshippers sincerely seek His favor through their worship and obedience. «وقوله: {يريدون وجهه} أي: يبتغون بذلك العمل وجه الله الكريم، فهم مخلصون فيما هم فيه من العبادات والطاعات»
#144 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Neither the Prophet nor these worshippers answer for one another; Ibn Kathir compares Noah’s response that their account belongs to God. «أي: إنما حسابهم على الله، عز وجل، وليس علي من حسابهم من شيء، كما أنه ليس عليهم من حسابي من شيء»
#145 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Seeking God’s face means that these people sincerely seek His favor through their worship and obedience. «وقوله: {فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين} أي: إن فعلت هذا والحالة هذه»
#146 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Neither the Prophet nor these worshippers answer for one another; Ibn Kathir compares Noah’s response that their account belongs to God. «قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا أسباط -هو ابن محمد -حدثنا أشعث، عن كردوس، عن ابن مسعود قال»
#147 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · خباب · reports · Khabbab says al-Aqra and Uyayna disdained the poor believers and sought an exclusive meeting with the Prophet; Gabriel revealed the command not to expel them, and the Prophet discarded their written pledge. «عن خباب في قول الله، عز وجل: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} قال: جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي»
#148 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Do not drive away people who invoke God morning and evening seeking His face; keep them close as companions, as also commanded in 18:28. «أي: لا تبعد هؤلاء المتصفين بهذه الصفة عنك، بل اجعلهم جلساءك وأخصاءك»
#149 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Al-Hakim grades Sa’d’s report about six Companions according to the criteria of al-Bukhari and Muslim; Ibn Hibban also transmits its route. «رواه الحاكم في مستدركه من طريق سفيان، وقال: على شرط الشيخين»
#150 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · reports · Ibn Kathir says Ibn Jarir also transmits the earlier report through Asbat. «ورواه ابن جرير، من حديث أسباط، به. (7)»
#151 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Ibn Kathir calls the report strange because this verse is Meccan whereas al-Aqra and Uyayna converted long after the Hijra. «وهذا حديث غريب، فإن هذه الآية مكية، والأقرع بن حابس وعيينة إنما أسلما بعد الهجرة بدهر»

#152 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · سعد · reports · Sa’d says the verse concerned six Companions, including Ibn Masud, who arrived early and drew near to hear the Prophet; Quraysh objected to their proximity. «نزلت هذه الآية في ستة من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، منهم ابن مسعود»
#153 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Those the Prophet must not drive away are poor Muslims, devoted to their Lord in contrast to unbelievers who call on powerless beings. «عكس ما عليه الكفار في دعاء من لا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا»
#154 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Morning and evening may mean both ends of each day, the two daily prayers, or continuous worship; their long constancy indicates sincerity rather than ostentation. «في طرفي النهار مطلقا أو بصلاتيهما أو يكون كناية عن الدوام»
#155 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The wealthy polytheists promised to follow Muhammad if he expelled his humble companions, whom they disparaged as insincere and driven by need. «وعدوه صلى الله عليه وسلم الاتباع إن طرد من تبعه ممن يأنفون من مجالستهم»
#156 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The Prophet has no stake in worldly gain from expelling the poor or accepting the rich; his mission calls people away from worldly life. «التي هو مبعوث للتنفير عنها»
#157 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The denial of responsibility for one another's account means the Prophet sees only outward conduct; he need not expel them over a fear that they are insincere or that they burden him. «ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء»
#158 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · An alternative reading of the denial of mutual accounting, linked to 18:28, concerns provision: the Prophet's invitation is for the afterlife, and neither the poor nor the Prophet depends on the other's provision. «يعني أن دعاءك إلى الله إنما مداره الأمر الأخروي»
#159 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · reports · The author adduces lexicons and usage showing that hisab can mean sufficiency or provision: 78:36 gives an abundant gift; the verb can mean feeding to satisfaction; and a report from Simak says hosts did not honor their guest. «صاحب القاموس وغيره : الحساب : الكافي»
#160 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · أبو عبيد الهروي · reports · Abu Ubayd explains ahsabtuhu as giving someone enough until he says, “That suffices me.” «أي أعطيته الكفاية حتى قال»
#161 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · reports · The phrase “without account” in 2:212 means without stinting or constriction; Ibn Faris likewise glosses ahsabtuhu as giving enough or what satisfies. «بغير تقتير وتضييق , وفي حديث سماك»
#162 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Expelling the poor would be unjustly putting things out of place and would not make the wealthy polytheists believe; guidance belongs to God alone. «وليس هدايتهم إلا إلينا»
#163 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · God tested groups through the Prophet's appointment and through differences of faith, wealth, and poverty; elites scorned the poor as unworthy of God's favor. «بالتخصيص بالإيمان والغنى والفقر ونحو ذلك» [filed under 6:52-53]
#164 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The elite's objection anticipates their later demand to receive what God's messengers received; God alone knows who merits preference through gratitude. «فالآية ناظرة إلى ما يأتي في هذه السورة من قوله تعالى» [filed under 6:52-53]
#165 DURR-FULL d.911 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslim companions such as Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, and Khabbab so that they might follow him; the warning verse was revealed. «عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال مر الملأ من قريش على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده صهيب وعمار وبلال وخباب»
#166 DURR-FULL d.911 · عكرمة · reports · Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have Muhammad expel poor and enslaved followers so they would join; Umar suggested testing their request, then verses about not expelling the believers were revealed. «عن عكرمة قال مشى عتبة بن ربيعة وشيبة بن ربيعة وقرظة بن عبد عمر وبن نوفل» [filed under 6:52, 6:53]
#167 SUYUTI-LUBAB d.911 · خباب · reports · Khabbab reports that Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers such as Suhayb, Bilal, Ammar, and Khabbab when Arab delegations arrived; the verse forbidding their expulsion was revealed. «جاء الأقرع ابن حابس وعيينة بن حصن فوجدا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع صهيب وبلال وعمار وخباب قاعدا في ناس من الضعفاء»
#168 SUYUTI-LUBAB d.911 · ابن كثير · rejects · Ibn Kathir calls the report unusual because the verse is Meccan while Aqra and Uyayna converted much later, after the Hijra. «قال ابن كثير هذا حديث غريب فإن الآية مكية والأقرع وعيينة إنما أسلما بعد الهجرة بدهر»
#169 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · ‘Seeking His face’ is circumstantial to ‘they call’; it stresses that sincerity is the essential point of supplication. «يدعونه تعالى مخلصين له وقيد الدعاء بالإخلاص تنبيها على أنه ملاك الأمر»
#170 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · A Persian couplet says worship is good when intention is sincere; without that, it is like a kernel-less grain. «عبادت بإخلاص نيت نكوست وكرنه ه آيد زبى مغزوست»
#171 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Seeking God's face is among the strongest grounds for honor and is incompatible with expelling poor worshippers. «من أقوى موجبات الإكرام المنافي للأبعاد»
#172 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Quraysh not only disparaged poor believers' status but alleged their faith was false and that they gathered for food and clothing; God rejects this as grounds for expulsion. «في طعن فقراء المسلمين على وصفهم بكونهم موالي ومساكين بل طعنوا في إيمانهم»
#173 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The Prophet must judge by their outward mark of piety; any hidden defect in faith harms only them, not him, so he should welcome and nurture them. «ليس عليك إلا اعتبار ظاهر حالهم وهو اتسامهم بسمة المتقين»
#174 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The repeated denial of responsibility emphasizes that their reckoning is no concern of the Prophet, just as his is no concern of theirs. «مع أن الجواب قد تم بما قبله للمبالغة في بيان انتفاء كون حسابهم عليه»
#175 BURSEVI d.1127 · أبو السعود · reports · Abū al-Suʿūd says the repeated phrase emphasizes the point by pairing it with the uncontroversial reverse; ‘then you expel them’ answers the prohibition's logic. «قال المولى أبو السعود : وذكر قوله تعالى»
#176 BURSEVI d.1127 · السري السقطي · reports · Al-Sarī al-Saqaṭī says he found Bahlūl in a cemetery; Bahlūl replied that the dead do not harm him or gossip when he is away. «خرجت يوما إلى المقابر فإذا ببهلول فقلت له أي شيء تصنع هنا»
#177 BURSEVI d.1127 · بهلول · reports · Bahlūl left when hungry and recited that hunger is a pious act and prolonged hunger will eventually be followed by satisfaction. «أجالس قوما لا يؤذونني وإن غبت لا يغتابونني»
#178 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · A king's parable shows God adorning chosen lovers with righteous deeds and pure states: they need not display themselves to ordinary people, since God knows and their rank will be seen at the great gathering. «فهذا مثل من وفقهم الله تعالى للأعمال الصالحة والأحوال الزكية ولا حاجة لهم»
#179 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · A Persian couplet contrasts the noble servants of God with the speaker's group as wretched slaves. «أولئك خدام كرام وسادة ونحن عبيد السوء بئس عبيد»
#180 BURSEVI d.1127 · reports · Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor wool-clad believers such as Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, Bilāl, and Salmān so they could retain his company and status before Arab visitors. «حين رأوا في مجلسه الشريف فقراء المؤمنين»
#181 BURSEVI d.1127 · رسول الله · reports · The Prophet refused to expel believers, though he considered separating them to attract Quraysh; revelation taught that religion does not privilege the rich over the poor. «ما أنا بطارد المؤمنين»
#182 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Expulsion means removal; morning and evening remembrance signifies continuity, and whoever remembers continually remains with God. «الطرد الإبعاد وبالفارسية»
#183 BURSEVI d.1127 · النبي · reports · The Prophet says, ‘I am the companion of whoever remembers Me.’ «أنا جليس من ذكرني»
#184 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The poor worshippers seek God's face and pleasure alone, not worldly aims. «بذكرهم وعبادتهم {وجهه} تعالى ورضاه لا شيئا من أغراض الدنيا»
#185 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · ‘Thus We tested them’ points to God's giving poor believers precedence in religion by granting faith despite their poor worldly condition, while the rich had worldly precedence. «ذلك إشارة إلى مصدر ما بعده من الفعل»
#186 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The prefixed kāf intensifies the demonstrative: God tried them with a complete and remarkable trial. «والكاف مقحمة لتأكيد ما أفاده اسم الإشارة من الفخامة»
#187 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · After commanding the Prophet to warn the people who may become pious, God forbids doing so in a way that would lead him to expel the poor believers. «لما أمر النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بانذار المذكورين لعلهم ينتظمون في سلك المتقين نهى»
#188 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · reports · Some accounts suggest the warning and no-expulsion verses came down together, while others do not indicate that. «ويفهم من بعض الروايات أن الآيتين نزلتا معا»
#189 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · ابن مسعود · reports · Ibn Masud reports Quraysh leaders seeing Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab, and other poor Muslims with the Prophet and demanding their expulsion, promising they might then follow him; the Quran was revealed concerning this. «مر الملأ من قريش على»
#190 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · خباب · reports · Khabbab reports that al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna looked down on the poor believers and demanded private access for tribal leaders, promising to meet the Prophet with the poor later; after Gabriel delivered the verse, the Prophet called the believers to him and then stayed with them when rising. «جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينة بن حصن الفزاري»
#191 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · عكرمة · reports · Ikrima reports that Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have Muhammad expel poor slaves and allies so they would follow him; Umar suggested doing so temporarily, and verses warning and identifying the grateful were revealed, after which Umar apologized. «مشى عتبة وشيبة أبنا ربيعة وقرظة بن عبد عمرو»
<<end of notes for 6_52_c2>>

item.text: The middle batches contain the main relevant traditions: readings of the morning term, the evening term’s sense, and whether the phrase means specific periods or continual worship. I’m mapping those to claim 4b; the account-clause grammar and occasion-of-revelation reports do not reach a page claim.
